titleEn: Wash Off the Mud, Then Hold the Bread!

pages.text: Pongi dug in the mud on the bank with her paws. "Soft and squishy! What fun!" Mom, wearing her headscarf, called from the house. "The bread is ready!" "Bread! I'll eat, then play again!" Pongi's paws were covered in mud.
Pongi grabbed the bread with muddy paws. A brown paw print appeared on it. "Wash your paws!" said Mom. "Too much trouble! The bread will get cold!" said Pongi. Munch, munch.
After she ate the bread, her tummy rumbled. It began to ache. "Oh, my tummy..." Pongi sat down and curled up. Mom hurried over and rubbed her back.
Mom looked at her paws. "Tiny wrigglers you can't see live in the mud. They hopped onto the bread and went into your tummy." "What can I do?" asked Pongi. Mom took her paws. "To the water tub!"
They stood beside the water tub near the doorway. Mom sang, "Just three steps to wash your paws! One, splash in the water!" Pongi dipped both paws in. The mud loosened and turned the water brown.
"Two, bubble up with soap!" Mom gave her the soap. Pongi rubbed her paws together. Five big clumps of bubbles puffed up. Her paws disappeared under the white foam. "I can't see my paws!"
"Three, rinse and rub between your paws!" Mom poured water. The tiny wrigglers washed away. Her paws were clean. Pongi thumped her tail on the floor. "Wash off the mud, then hold the bread!"
Pongi picked up fresh bread. There wasn't a mark on it. Yum! Her tummy didn't hurt anymore. Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, walked past. "Ha, ha! Your paws are whiter than the bread."
The next day, Pongi went to the water tub first. "Paws first, before eating!" She sang, "One, splash in the water! Two, bubble up with soap! Three, rub between your paws!"

Mom held Pongi's two clean paws in her own. "These paws did it all!" With clean paws, the tiny wrigglers can't ride on the bread, and her tummy won't hurt. Pongi called, "Wash off the mud, then hold the bread!"
